Ivy (CS): Heads-up: CascadePay renewal demo in 4 days. They want a single-page runbook for demo day: fast warmup, lightweight fallback, and an in-demo survey. Can eng/sre/solutions sign off?

Noah (Eng): Short customer steps: 1) Prefill 10m before demo with ~40 common prompts to seed KV cache. 2) Start a transient warm pool sized to their peak concurrency. 3) Enable a small-quant fallback model and a circuit-breaker to auto-route if queueing appears. Prefill example (customer): `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prefill -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"tenant_id":"cascadepay-prod","prompts":["acct overview","recent tx"]}'`

Ivy (CS): They expect ~150 concurrent demo flows. Any quick sizing guidance? :thinking_face:

Pri (SRE): For 150 concurrent: set warm_pool 6 per shard, batch_target 8, and temporary autoscale +1. Add temporary alerts during the window: queue_depth > 45 or p95_latency > 800ms. Circuit-breaker rule: if queue_depth > 60 for 1m, route to fallback.

Ola (Solutions): I'll run a 20-min smoke 24h prior and collect 6 sample prompts per demo path. Post-demo survey: Q1) Latency acceptable? (Yes/No). Q2) Any output issues? (optional). We capture responses in the account ticket and link to traces.

toolbot: deployment: warm-pool-update -> canary (id: c-2298). ETA 2m.

Noah (Eng): Staging quick check: KV hit rate jumped to 76% after prefill; cached p95 ~130ms. Will add circuit-breaker steps to runbook.

Pri (SRE): I'll add runbook snippets for on-call: how to toggle circuit-breaker, how to scale manually, and where to find tenant traces.

Ivy (CS): Action items: @Noah add prefill snippet to the one-pager; @Pri add alerts and circuit-breaker; @Ola run smoke and send survey link. I'll confirm demo time with CascadePay PM and mark renewal risk = Monitor.

Noah (Eng): Confirmed. Closing this thread after the smoke and demo summary attached to the renewal ticket.
